authors: Erfan Baghaei Potraghloo, Seyedarmin Azizi, Souvik Kundu, and Massoud Pedram

breakthroughAssessment.justification: This paper presents a strong contribution by introducing Top-H decoding, a theoretically grounded sampling method that effectively balances creativity and coherence in LLM text generation. It formalizes the problem as an NP-hard entropy-constrained mass maximization problem and proposes an efficient greedy approximation. Extensive empirical evaluations demonstrate consistent state-of-the-art performance, especially at higher temperatures, outperforming established methods like min-p and top-p by significant margins (e.g., up to 25.63% accuracy improvement). The method also offers robustness to temperature scaling and provides a clear path for future research in dynamic alpha adaptation and approximation guarantees, marking it as highly useful to the sub-field.

coreProblem.concreteExample: Min-p sampling, for instance, relies on a single top token's probability to estimate confidence. This often leads to over-truncation in sparse probability distributions and under-truncation in dense distributions, failing to effectively utilize the overall shape of the probability distribution for optimal token selection.
coreProblem.statement: Large language models (LLMs) struggle to balance two competing objectives in open-ended text generation: fostering diversity and creativity while preserving logical coherence. Existing truncation-based sampling techniques (e.g., temperature scaling, top-p, min-p) often fail to effectively incorporate the model's confidence, leading to suboptimal trade-offs, particularly at higher temperatures where coherence degrades.
whyItMatters: Enables LLMs to generate text that is simultaneously more creative and coherent, addressing a long-standing challenge in open-ended text generation.
Improves the robustness of LLM outputs across varying temperature settings, making them more reliable for diverse applications.
Provides a principled, theoretically-grounded approach to text generation sampling, moving beyond heuristic methods.

evaluationHighlights: Top-H consistently outperforms existing sampling methods (min-p, top-p, top-k, eta-sampling) in balancing creativity and coherence.
Demonstrates remarkable robustness to temperature scaling, preserving effectiveness at high temperatures where traditional methods significantly degrade.
Achieves up to 25.63% higher accuracy compared to min-p on creative writing benchmarks with LLaMA3.1-8B.
Maintains strong accuracy on reasoning datasets (GPQA, GSM8K) even at high temperatures, with significant accuracy improvements over baselines.
Exhibits negligible computational overhead, performing as efficiently as top-p and min-p (as low as 0.8% overhead).
Outperforms Mirostat, another entropy-aware baseline, by +13.3% on MT-Bench and +4.3% on GPQA averaged across models and temperatures.

evaluationSetup.setting: Open-ended text generation, creative writing, reasoning (Chain-of-Thought tasks), human-aligned evaluations using LLM-as-a-judge framework.

mainTakeaways: Top-H decoding consistently outperforms established sampling methods (min-p, top-p, top-k, eta-sampling) in balancing creativity and coherence across various LLMs and tasks.
The method demonstrates superior robustness to temperature scaling, maintaining high performance at increased temperatures where other baselines experience significant degradation.

Top-H provides substantial accuracy improvements on reasoning and QA benchmarks (e.g., up to 25.63% on creative writing benchmarks, +7.36% on GPQA) and achieves higher human-aligned evaluation scores for creative writing.
Top-H introduces negligible computational overhead, making it a practically efficient solution despite addressing an NP-hard problem.
The greedy approach of Top-H is empirically shown to closely approximate the optimal solution to the entropy-constrained mass maximization problem.

explanation: Top-H decoding is theoretically grounded by formulating the trade-off between creativity and coherence as an entropy-constrained minimum divergence (ECMD) problem, which is proven to be equivalent to an NP-hard entropy-constrained mass maximization (ECMM) problem.
It provides a computationally efficient greedy algorithm that approximates the solution to the ECMM problem, enabling practical deployment while adhering to the entropy constraint.

Unlike prior heuristic methods, Top-H dynamically adjusts its entropy threshold based on the evolving entropy of the token distribution, allowing adaptive control over randomness and effective incorporation of model confidence.
keyNovelty.main: Top-H decoding, a novel sampling method that dynamically selects a subset of tokens for text generation by maintaining minimal divergence from the original distribution under an upper-bounded entropy constraint, thereby balancing creativity and coherence.

keyTerms.definition: Sampling methods that select a subset of tokens from the full vocabulary to generate the next token, typically based on probability thresholds (e.g., top-k, top-p, min-p).
A sampling strategy that selects the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds a predefined threshold p, aiming to reduce the sampling space.
A dynamic sampling strategy that scales a base probability score threshold by the probability of the top-1 token, restricting the sample space more aggressively when the model is confident.

An optimization problem to determine a subset of tokens that minimizes the Jensen-Shannon divergence from the original probability distribution, subject to an entropy constraint on the selected subset's distribution.

An optimization problem, proven equivalent to ECMD, that aims to maximize the sum of probabilities of tokens in a selected subset, subject to an entropy constraint on the subset's renormalized distribution. This problem is NP-hard.

comparisonToPriorWork: Traditional temperature scaling can lead to incoherent text at high temperatures due to indiscriminate exploration, whereas Top-H maintains coherence by adaptively constraining randomness.
Top-k sampling's hard cutoff is insensitive to context and can arbitrarily exclude plausible tokens, which Top-H avoids by considering the overall distribution shape and entropy.

Top-p (nucleus) sampling can include low-probability tokens at high temperatures, harming coherence, and lacks awareness of the model's confidence based purely on cumulative probability. Top-H explicitly controls entropy and adapts to model uncertainty.

Min-p sampling relies solely on the top-1 token's probability for confidence, often overlooking broader distributional features, leading to over- or under-truncation. Top-H addresses this by considering the entire probability distribution's entropy.

Entropy-based methods like eta-sampling and Mirostat often require extensive hyperparameter tuning or introduce significant runtime overhead. Top-H offers a balance of efficiency and effectiveness with minimal overhead and a single hyperparameter (alpha).
limitations: As a greedy solution to an NP-hard problem, Top-H does not provide general competitive guarantees that apply across a broad range of distributions.
The hyperparameter alpha, which controls the entropy threshold, is currently tuned manually, though the method exhibits robustness to its variation.
Future research is needed to design an algorithm that offers a provable approximation ratio and can dynamically adapt the entropy threshold alpha.

modeling.label: Conditional probability $q_i$ over subset $S$
modeling.value: $q_i = \begin{cases} p_i / \Gamma_S & v_i \in S \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$, where $\Gamma_S = \sum_{v_i \in S} p_i$

modeling.label: Jensen-Shannon Divergence
modeling.value: $JSD(p \| q) = \frac{1}{2} D_{KL}(p \| M) + \frac{1}{2} D_{KL}(q \| M)$, where $M = \frac{1}{2}(p+q)$

pipelineFlow: 1. Initialize: Given a probability mass function $p=(p_1, \dots, p_n)$ and an entropy threshold coefficient $\alpha \in (0,1)$.
2. Sort tokens: Sort all candidate tokens in descending order of their probabilities ($p_1 \ge p_2 \ge \dots \ge p_n$).
3. Iterative Addition: Initialize an empty selected token set $S$ and $H(q)=0$. Iteratively add tokens from the sorted list to $S$.
4. Entropy Calculation: After each token addition, compute the updated distribution $q$ over $S$ and its Shannon entropy $H(q)$.
5. Constraint Check: If the calculated $H(q)$ exceeds the dynamic entropy threshold $\alpha \cdot H(p)$, the last added token is removed from $S$, and the algorithm terminates.
6. Return: The final set $S$ of selected tokens is used for sampling the next token.

problemDefinition.label: Entropy-Constrained Minimum Divergence (ECMD)
problemDefinition.value: $\min_S JSD(q \| p) \text{ subject to } H(q) \le \alpha H(p)$

problemDefinition.label: Entropy-Constrained Mass Maximization (ECMM)
problemDefinition.value: $\max_S \sum_{i \in S} p_i \text{ subject to } H(q) \le \alpha H(p)$

technicalDetails.reproducibility: The code for Top-H decoding is publicly available at https://github.com/ErfanBaghaei/Top-H-Decoding. Experiments were conducted using PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers library.

thesis: Top-H decoding provides a theoretically grounded and computationally efficient greedy algorithm to balance creativity and coherence in open-ended text generation, outperforming existing sampling methods, especially at high temperatures, by addressing the entropy-constrained mass maximization problem.
title: Top-H Decoding: Adapting the Creativity and Coherence with Bounded Entropy in Text Generation
